title: Correlative Light X-ray and Electron Microscopy of Endothelial Cells in Mouse Tissue
author: Reglero-Real, Pérez-Gutiérrez, et al.

steps.title: Rinse aldehyde‑fixed tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the tissue to a plastic 35 mm petri dish containing 0.1 M phosphate buffer (PB) and rinse three times with ~2 mL 0.1 M PB for 5 min each.

steps.title: Fix tissue with reduced OsO₄
steps.instruction: Replace the PB with 2 % reduced osmium tetroxide, place the closed dish in the PELCO BioWave Pro microwave (using the vacuum chamber), remove the lid and run the microwave on/off cycles for a total of 14 min as specified in the program.

steps.title: Rinse tissue in fume hood
steps.instruction: Rinse once with 0.1 M PB, then rinse with distilled water (ddH₂O) until the solution is clear.

steps.title: Microwave wash with ddH₂O
steps.instruction: Wash the tissue twice with ddH₂O in the microwave using steps 10–11 of the supplied program; rinse thoroughly to remove residual OsO₄.

steps.title: Pause (osmicated tissue storage)
steps.instruction: Store the osmicated tissue in ddH₂O at 4 °C if needed, but complete the preparation as soon as possible to avoid damage.

steps.title: Treat tissue with TCH
steps.instruction: Filter 1 % thiocarbohydrazide (TCH) through a 0.22 µm syringe filter, remove ddH₂O from the tissue, add the filtered TCH, place the closed dish in the microwave vacuum chamber, remove the lid and incubate for 14 min (steps 12–18) with the program set to 40 °C.

steps.title: Rinse tissue after TCH
steps.instruction: Rinse in the fume hood with ddH₂O until the solution becomes clear.

steps.title: Microwave wash after TCH
steps.instruction: Wash twice with ddH₂O in the microwave using steps 20–21 of the program; use a fresh petri dish for the next step to avoid grayish TCH film.

steps.title: Treat tissue with second OsO₄
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 2 % OsO₄ in a new petri dish, transfer the tissue, place the closed dish in the microwave vacuum chamber, remove the lid and run microwave cycles for 14 min (steps 22–28).

steps.title: Rinse after second OsO₄
steps.instruction: Rinse with ddH₂O until the solution is clear.

steps.title: Microwave wash after second OsO₄
steps.instruction: Wash twice with ddH₂O in the microwave using steps 30–31 of the program.

steps.title: Stain with uranyl acetate
steps.instruction: Replace ddH₂O with 1 % uranyl acetate, place the closed dish in the microwave vacuum chamber, remove the lid and incubate for 14 min (steps 32–38) with the program set to 40 °C.

steps.title: Rinse after uranyl acetate
steps.instruction: Rinse with ddH₂O until clear.

steps.title: Microwave wash after uranyl acetate
steps.instruction: Wash twice with ddH₂O in the microwave using steps 40–41 of the program.

steps.title: Stain with lead aspartate
steps.instruction: Exchange ddH₂O for lead aspartate, place the closed dish in the microwave vacuum chamber, remove the lid and incubate for 14 min (steps 42–48) with the program set to 50 °C.

steps.title: Rinse after lead aspartate
steps.instruction: Rinse with ddH₂O until clear.

steps.title: Microwave wash after lead aspartate
steps.instruction: Wash twice with ddH₂O in the microwave using steps 50–51 of the program.

steps.title: Pause (post‑staining storage)
steps.instruction: Store the sample in ddH₂O at 4 °C if needed, but finish the protocol promptly to avoid damage.

steps.title: Dehydrate with graded ethanol
steps.instruction: Prepare 30 %, 50 %, 70 % and 90 % ethanol (in ddH₂O). Incubate the sample in each concentration for 30 min at 20–24 °C with gentle shaking. Then incubate sequentially in 99.8 % ethanol (straight from the bottle) and 100 % dry ethanol for 30 min each, still at 20–24 °C with agitation.

steps.title: Propylene oxide incubation
steps.instruction: Transfer the sample to a glass, polypropylene or aluminum vial containing propylene oxide and incubate twice for 15 min each (avoid polyethylene containers).

steps.title: Prepare Durcupan resin
steps.instruction: Mix Durcupan resin according to the Materials and Equipment section; this can be done while the sample is undergoing dehydration and propylene oxide steps.

steps.title: Infiltrate with 50 % Durcupan
steps.instruction: Make a 1:1 mixture of propylene oxide and Durcupan resin, exchange the propylene oxide for this 50 % Durcupan solution, and incubate the sample for 12–24 h in a fume hood or desiccator with the lid open to allow gradual evaporation of propylene oxide.

steps.title: Infiltrate with 100 % Durcupan (first)
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 100 % Durcupan resin, transfer the sample to an aluminum dish containing the fresh resin, briefly place the dish on a hot plate to lower viscosity and mix any residual resin, then infiltrate for 2 h at 20–24 °C (rocker or rotator may be used).

steps.title: Exchange with fresh 100 % Durcupan
steps.instruction: Move the sample to a new aluminum dish with fresh 100 % Durcupan resin and briefly heat on a hot plate to reduce viscosity before proceeding.

steps.title: Flat‑embed the tissue
steps.instruction: Cut a top Aclar film sheet to just cover the tissue; prepare thin Aclar strips as spacers. Place a bottom Aclar sheet and spacers on a glass slide, adjust chamber height, lay the infiltrated tissue (imaged side down) onto the bottom sheet, add fresh resin, then gently place the top Aclar sheet over it, removing excess resin and avoiding bubbles or pressure.

steps.title: Polymerize resin
steps.instruction: Place the flat‑embedded sample in an oven at 60 °C and polymerize for 48 h.

steps.title: Remove Aclar films
steps.instruction: After cooling, take the block out of the oven and carefully peel away both Aclar films.
